A1.1          | Nothing sets it off — this is a formatting convention (reference table), see A3
A1.2          | A zone percentage value, a zone range's two bounds, an extreme zone's operator and bound, a distance value, a press duration value — all integers to format as text
A1.3          | Five formatted text strings: zone percentage text, zone range text, extreme zone text, distance text, press duration text

A1.7          | N/A — no trigger (reference table)
A1.8          | N/A — no trigger (reference table)
A2.text.1     | Percentage: integer+NBSP+"%" (e.g. "50 %"); Range: bound–bound+space+"bpm" with en dash (e.g. "94–112 bpm"); Extreme: operator+space+integer+space+"bpm" (e.g. "< 94 bpm", "> 150 bpm"); Distance: integer+space+"m", no thousands separator (e.g. "1000 m"); Duration: integer+space+"ms" (e.g. "700 ms")
A2.text.2     | gap: block does not say what the text becomes if the underlying value is absent
A3.1          | All five formats given in full: zone percentage, zone range, extreme zone, distance, press duration (see A2.text.1)
A3.2          | gap: block does not say who/what consults these formats
A3.3          | gap: block does not say what happens if a value to format is missing or invalid
A3.4          | gap: block does not say whether these formats can change after delivery
A4.1          | Every name used (zone percentage, zone range, extreme zone, distance, press duration) is a format the block defines itself
A4.2          | N/A — the block cites no other block or external description, only its own format definitions
A4.3          | N/A — no comparative qualifier used ("extreme" names a category here, it is not compared to another term)
